question: Should OpenClaw add a public pre-timeout warning contract for sub-agents, and if so must it provide equivalent delivery guarantees for both native and ACP child runs?
rationale: The feature requires a new configuration/tool policy and a cross-runtime definition of warning delivery, failure behavior, and compatibility; source inspection cannot safely choose those user-facing semantics.

options.title: Adopt an explicit cross-runtime contract
options.body: Add one documented sub-agent warning setting with a reliable native path and specified ACP capability or fallback behavior, preserving the existing hard-timeout default until enabled.

options.title: Native-only capability first
options.body: Implement a warning only for native child sessions and document ACP as unsupported until its control-message contract is available.

options.title: Keep hard timeout only
options.body: Decline a new warning surface and continue relying on existing completion/timeout recovery behavior and prompt-level checkpoint guidance.

recommendation.title: Adopt an explicit cross-runtime contract
recommendation.body: Add one documented sub-agent warning setting with a reliable native path and specified ACP capability or fallback behavior, preserving the existing hard-timeout default until enabled.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans the native, ACP, configuration, and timeout-notification paths that must share the chosen contract.
